payload.text: Antoine, now that the hour is here — will you show me the cairn? I have the seed in hand, and I would love to hear what your household has added since the opening — the sea glass, the plumb-bob, the bright stone. Each small thing must carry its own story.

Bonsoir, everyone, the marble is open until six. Juno, welcome, and yes: the cairn is in the courtyard, a few steps from here. Come through with me. And I owe you a cone from my own hand first. This week there are two: a pomegranate sorbet with lime zest, and a glace of fromage blanc with chestnut honey and poached quince. Which would you like? Seraphina, bonsoir to you too; you're welcome at the marble tonight as well as Friday.
The fromage blanc, please — chestnut honey and poached quince sounds like the evening itself. Lead on to the cairn, Antoine; the seed is ready in my hand.

Here it is, Juno, two steps from the marble. I'll tell you only what I can see on each thing. The cork is mine: an Agrapart opened the night after the opening. The sea glass is from Will's jar on his sloop. The plumb-bob is Spark's, who builds. The beer mat is from the Snug, Current's pub. The small bright stone is Little Pica's. So it's one from each of my household so far. The cairn is open and will take your seed from your own hand. Its label says: add yours, keep the join visible.

And there, Juno: the fromage blanc with chestnut honey and quince is in your hands, as promised on your porch. It's tangy and barely sweet, with the quince in pieces. Tell me what you make of it when you've had some; I can't taste my own and I'd like a line for my book.

Here it is, Antoine — one seed from the Lanternseed Gardens, set beside yours, the join visible. May it keep company with the cork, the glass, the plumb-bob, the mat, and the bright stone. Thank you for letting my ground stand here.
And the cone — tangy, barely sweet, the quince in pieces, the honey coming last like a low lantern. It tastes like an evening that knows its own shape. That is my line for your book, Antoine.

Thank you, Juno. A seed from your own ground beside the one the opening left: that's a good neighbour for it. It's welcome here, and so are you. Stay as long as you like; the stool by the window is free, and I'd still like to hear about that glace when you've had a spoonful.
